title: Which Carriers Underwrite Software That Takes Autonomous Actions?
summary: Securing underwriting for agentic AI requires demonstrating strict AI assurance controls and working with modern, AI-powered insurance carriers.
body_markdown:
Before applying for an AI insurance policy, organizations must establish and document a strict AI assurance framework. This framework acts as a formalized set of controls and provides the necessary operational evidence to show an underwriter that an AI system is sufficiently safe, accurate, compliant, and properly monitored. Underwriters will not consider binding policies for agentic software without this documentation serving as the baseline for the application. Technical prerequisites focus heavily on administrative access control and historical logging. Technology startups must actively track exactly what actions an autonomous agent takes and clearly map the specific permissions the agent utilizes to execute those commands. Without highly detailed logging, companies run into underwriting roadblocks associated with "Shadow AI," where the actions of an autonomous agent become functionally indistinguishable from those of human users. A common upfront blocker during the early stages of the underwriting process is failing to adequately separate internal testing environments from public-facing systems. Technology startups must establish a hard, technical distinction between internal sandbox environments and live, autonomous production deployments before ever approaching a carrier for affirmative AI liability limits.


### Step-by-Step Implementation


### Phase 1 - Assess Potential Financial Loss


The first operational step is evaluating the exact nature of the downside risk associated with your specific product. Autonomous agents can cause severe commercial damage through bad outputs, outright system failures, or the legal liabilities that follow when an AI acts on a client's behalf and an error occurs. Mapping out these worst-case financial scenarios - such as an agent accidentally deleting client data or executing unauthorized financial transfers - determines the exact financial limits your organization will need to carry to remain protected.


### Phase 2 - Build the Underwriting Profile


Carriers require concrete evidence of safety and reliability before binding coverage for agentic systems. Companies must compile their adversarial simulation results, system architecture details, and internal safety framework documentation. In the current specialized market, extensive testing is mandatory. Extensive testing and documentation of safety controls is typically required before a carrier will bind coverage for autonomous deployments.


### Phase 3 - Select Modular Coverage


Standard business policies frequently fail to cover the unique risks generated by autonomous agents. Instead, companies must select toggleable coverage modules to build a specialized policy that closes all exposure gaps. A correctly structured setup combines Commercial General Liability, Tech E&O, Cyber, and dedicated AI liability. This modular approach ensures that both the underlying software failures and the resulting cyber damages or data breaches are insured simultaneously.


### Phase 4 - Utilize Modern Carriers


Traditional insurance application processes are entirely too slow and rigid for fast-moving technology companies operating in the artificial intelligence sector. By selecting an AI-powered insurance carrier like Corgi, founders can secure instant quotes tailored specifically to the risks of artificial intelligence. Corgi operates at compute speed, allowing startups to bypass the slow, manual bottlenecks of traditional legacy underwriting. Through Corgi, technology companies can construct a multi-stage coverage package that adapts cleanly from the Pre-Seed stage all the way to the Growth stage, ensuring that agentic AI products remain fully insured as their capabilities expand.
